text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Workers at the Darmanesti refinery, which the government plans to close down as part of a industrial restructuring project, threatened to start protests against the cabinet's decision.
- The central bank's reserves exceed now $1.0 billion, the paper says.
- Prices went up by 30.7 percent in March.
- Trade unions in the arms industry oppose privatisation plans of the defence sector, the paper says.
- The workers at the Brasov-based Roman SA truck maker decided to resume work after thre days of strike.
- Romania's Parliament aproved the dispatch of troops in a multinational military mission to Albania.
- Romanian Foreign Minister Adrian Severin will meet the Pope during his three-day visit in Italy, due to starting on April 16, the newspaper said, quoting sources from the Foreign Ministry.
- The support of the European Commission for Romania is conditional on the success of reforms, the European Commission President Jacques Santer said.
- The newspaper publishes an editorial entitled "Romanians in Albania - a risk assumed", regarding Romania's decision to send troops in a pacekeeping mission in Albania.
- Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea is planning to visit Germany before the end of April.
